sections.heading: FAQs From East Orange Homeowners About Asphalt Shingles and Free Estimates

faqs.q: What is the difference between 3-tab and architectural shingles for an East Orange rental?

runs.v: Architectural shingles are multi-layer, last about 30 years, and rate up to 130 mph with the 6-nail pattern; 3-tab is a single flat layer that lasts about 20 years and rates near 60 mph, per ARMA and manufacturer guidance.

faqs.q: How many layers of shingles can my East Orange building carry?

runs.v: Two at most. The NJ Rehabilitation Subcode requires a full tear-off to bare deck when a roof is water-soaked or already carries 2 or more layers (N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4), and many multi-family roofs here were recovered before, so an inspection checks the layer count first.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for an asphalt shingle reroof in East Orange?

runs.v: Not on a detached one- or two-family home, where a reroof is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7. On commercial, larger multi-family, or attached buildings, the 25% rule applies: reroofing more than 25% of the roof in 12 months needs a permit.

faqs.q: Does an asphalt reroof on a Register-listed East Orange building need historic approval?

runs.v: Register listing alone places no restriction on a privately funded reroof, per the National Park Service; local historic designation is separate, so confirm the property's status with the city first.

faqs.q: Why does my East Orange walk-up keep losing shingles from the underside?

runs.v: Undersized attic ventilation lets trapped heat and moisture age the shingles from below; Newark Quality Roofing adds soffit intake and ridge exhaust toward the 1:150 ratio where the geometry allows.
